newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Electronics push Taiwan stocks up in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Electronics push Taiwan stocks up in late trade.

text.p: Bullish electronics pushed Taiwan stock index higher in late Friday's trade with investors pouring big funds into the red-hot sector, brokers said.

The technology shares were up 4.97 percent at 0320 GMT or 40 minutes before close, sending the overall index to 127.55 points or 1.32 percent higher at 9,759.97. Turnover was active at T$156.71 billion.
Several electronics stocks had risen to their seven-percent daily limit in just 15 minutes after the market opened, brokers said.
"This has further driven investors to pour money into the technology sector," said Alex Yang of National Securities.
Brokers said investors originally worried that the electronics sector might turn soft after a sharp rebound on Thursday.

The heavily weighted electronics rebounded well over six percent on Thursday after losing some 15 percent between July 17 and July 23 due to heavy profit-taking led by foreign institutional investors.
The sector rose more than 100 percent in the first half of 1997.
Chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductors was limit up at T$153, rising T$10, and its rival United Microelectronics had also risen to the seven-percent daily limit to T$128, gaining T$8.
Acer Sertek, an arm of computer giant Acer Inc, was limit up at T$99, rising T$6.5, while computer maker Mitac had soared to its daily limit by T$2.9 to T$45.7.
